m: To provoke hostility in someone.
t: Cousin of « antagoniste ». Don't antagonize the client.

m: Too poor to produce much or any vegetation; unproductive.
e: Old French baraigne (sterile, of land or women).
t: Think « bréhaigne » (old: sterile). Barren desert = désert aride.

m: To persuade by sustained coaxing or flattery.
e: French cajoler (to chatter like a jay), from gaiole (cage).
t: Same as « cajoler »: coax with sweet words.

m: A lament for the dead; a mournful song.
e: Latin dirige (direct!), the first word of the Office of the Dead.
t: Latin dirige (“guide”): opening of a funeral prayer. A dirge = funeral song.

m: Intoxicating; exhilarating.
t: Goes to your head: « grisant ». Heady perfume, heady days.

m: To criticize harshly.
t: Beat + beat: verbally. « Éreinter » a film.

m: A small, minor sin or fault.
t: Same as « peccadille »: a little pécher.

m: Extremely distasteful; unacceptable.
t: Same as « répugnant ».

m: To use deception to deprive of money or possessions.
t: Swindler: « escroc ».

m: Perceptible by touch; real and concrete.
t: Same as « tangible ».

m: Complete; not mixed with anything.
t: « Alliage »: no alloy. Unalloyed joy = joie pure.

m: To weaken; to offer lower prices than a competitor.
f: saper, mettre à mal; casser les prix
t: Cut from beneath: it « sape » the argument.

m: To persuade by flattery or coaxing.
e: Possibly German wedeln (to wag the tail, fawn).
t: A dog wagging its tail: wheedle a treat out of you.

m: Having a fear or dislike of strangers or foreigners.
t: Same as « xénophobe ».

m: Existing in thought rather than as a concrete thing.
t: Same as « abstrait ».

m: An action that causes offence.
e: Old French afronter (to slap in the face), Latin ad frontem.
t: Same as « affront »: a slap in the front/face.

m: To disturb or excite; to campaign.
t: Same as « agiter ».

m: To polish by rubbing.
e: Old French burnir (to make brown, polish), from brun.
t: « Brunir »: to polish metal until it shines. Burnish an image.

m: Making a pretence of shyness; reluctant to give details.
t: « Coi » (se tenir coi). Coy about the salary = évasif.

m: To express disapproval of; to belittle (self-deprecating).
t: Not depreciate (lose value). Self-deprecating humour belittles oneself: « autodérision ».

m: The feeling that someone is unworthy of respect.
e: Old French desdeignier, Latin dedignari (to reject as unworthy).
t: Same as « dédain ».

m: To go in different directions.
t: Same as « disperser ».

m: Exhibiting wildly uncontrolled emotion; extremely funny.
t: Hysterical laughter = fou rire. A hysterical comedy is hilarious.

m: A period of isolation to prevent the spread of disease.
t: Same as « quarantaine »: forty days (quarante).

m: To reject as invalid; to put an end to.
t: Casser! Quash a verdict = casser un jugement; quash a rebellion.

m: To argue about trivial matters.
e: Probably from Latin quibus (to whom), legal jargon pun.
t: Quibble = ergoter. Don't quibble over details.

m: To cause severe damage to.
t: Same as « ravager ».

m: High-pitched and piercing.
t: Hear the shriek: « strident ».

m: The use of clever but misleading arguments.
t: Same as « sophisme »: clever but misleading.

m: Skilled at gaining an advantage by deceit.
t: Wile E. Coyote. « Rusé ».

m: An attack on someone's reputation (usually: cast aspersions).
t: Sprinkle mud on someone's name: cast aspersions on.

m: Humorously indecent.
t: Rabelais! A bawdy tale = histoire grivoise.

m: To cooperate secretly for illegal ends.
t: Same as « collusion ».

m: To express sympathy or pity.
t: Commisérer. Share someone's misery.

m: An unexpected and awkward occurrence.
t: Straight from French « contretemps ».

m: A firmly held belief; a formal declaration of guilt.
t: « Conviction » = belief. Also a criminal conviction = condamnation.

m: To sing softly in a low voice.
t: Frank Sinatra, the crooner.

m: To remove from office; to testify under oath.
t: Same as « déposer »: put down the ruler.

m: The easing of strained relations.
t: Straight from French « détente ».

m: Unfashionable and drab.
t: Dull dress: « mal fagoté ».

m: A level or rank in an organization.
t: Same as « échelon »: upper echelons of management.

m: Listlessness arising from boredom.
t: Straight from French: « l'ennui » (stronger in English).

m: To speak or write at length on a subject.
t: Not « expatriate » (live abroad). Expatiate = « s'étendre » on a subject.

m: Filled with (something undesirable); causing anxiety.
t: Freight: loaded with. A fraught meeting is « chargé de tension ».

m: The point on which a lever rests; the pivot of an activity.
t: Archimède: the pivot of a lever.

m: Cheerful and lighthearted.
t: Jocund = jovial; same joke (jocus) root as « jouer ».

m: Quick and light in movement.
t: Nimble fingers: « agile ».

m: Giving the impression that something bad will happen.
t: An omen: « de mauvais augure ».

m: Looking or sounding bizarre or unfamiliar.
t: From outside the land: weird.

m: Deriving pleasure from inflicting pain.
t: Same as « sadique » — named for the French marquis.

m: To tolerate; to accept or follow (rules).
t: Can't abide = ne supporte pas. Abide by the rules = respecter.

m: A bold manner intended to impress; false courage.
t: Same as « bravade ».

m: Behaviour or manners; bearing.
t: Not « déportation »! Deportment = bearing, comportement.

m: To speak or perform without preparation.
t: Ex tempore: out of the moment.

m: (Of land) ploughed but left unplanted; inactive.
t: Jachère. A fallow period for the mind.

m: A deceptive movement intended to distract.
t: Same as « feinte » in boxing and fencing.

m: Conspicuously offensive; blatant.
t: « Flagrant délit »: caught in the act.

m: Uncalled for; lacking good reason.
t: Not 'free of charge' here: gratuit = for no reason. Gratuitous violence = violence gratuite, injustifiée.

m: To arouse curiosity; to plot secretly.
t: Same as « intriguer ».

m: Existing in name only; very small (of a fee).
t: For a nominal fee = une somme symbolique. Nominal leader: leader in name only.

m: Extremely unpleasant; repulsive.
t: Same as « odieux ».

m: Payment for work done.
t: Same as « rémunération ».

m: Untidy and dirty; careless.
t: Un « souillon ». A slovenly appearance.

m: An act of speaking one's thoughts aloud when alone.
t: Hamlet’s « To be or not to be ».

m: Vigour, spirit and style in writing or performance.
t: Same as « verve ».

m: Filled with horror or shock.
t: As if you've seen a ghost: « sidéré ».

m: To inform or tell someone of something.
e: French apprendre (to learn, to teach), past participle appris.
t: Not « apprécier »! Apprise = « mettre au courant ». Apprise him of the facts.

m: To charm or enchant; to deceive.
t: Guile: ruse. Beguiled by a smile = séduit. Also beguile into = tromper.

m: Showing insensitive disregard for others.
t: Un cal(lus) on the heart: thick skin.
